title: [Spec] Enable adaptive speculative decoding under DP attention (PR #35898)
quote: under skewed load `min` pins every rank to the lowest tier a neighbor wants, so a light rank can lose speculation it could afford
proves: SGLang disables adaptive draft depth under DP attention because ranks choosing different num_steps change the shape of the cross-rank MLP-sync all_gather and NCCL hangs. The PR agrees a tier by min() over ranks on the existing all_gather; 4xH200 tp4/dp2/ep4 EAGLE GSM8K: adaptive = fixed (116 tok/s at c1, 548 at c8, accept_len ~3.25). PR closed unmerged.
does_not_prove: No result on a low-acceptance or skewed workload; the cost of min-consensus (light ranks losing speculation) is stated, not measured. No per-rank speculation (different K per rank with shape padding) was tried.
bearing: Supports: per-DP-rank speculation depth under a lockstep collective is an open, acknowledged problem

title: [Spec] Stabilize the DP adaptive tier vote: shared EMA + min dwell (PR #39231)
quote: `min()` over 8 noisy per-rank EMAs sits below the mean at dp-rank BS~1, so alternating is the *steady state*, not an accident.
proves: GLM-5.2 tp8/dp8/ep8: min-of-8 DP tier vote thrashed ~1100 tier switches/h at c8 (298/h c16, 56/h c24), c16 ITL p95 +14% vs fixed. Fix (shared mean EMA over the all_gather + min dwell 50 batches) cut to 1 switch over the whole ladder; throughput -1.2% to +2.9% vs fixed EAGLE. Closed unmerged.
does_not_prove: Fix replaces min with a fleet mean, so every rank runs one tier; it does not let ranks with different acceptance run different depths. Single runs; no skewed-acceptance workload.
bearing: Supports: DP-wide speculation control is fragile; per-rank heterogeneity is averaged away, not exploited

title: Dynamic speculative decoding (vLLM docs)
quote: Each DP rank schedules independently, so ranks can pick different K values, causing DP collective divergence and deadlocks.
proves: vLLM maps concurrency ranges to K (example: K=3 at 1-64, K=1 at 65-128, K=0 at 129-512) and automatically disables num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size when DP is enabled, falling back to static K.
does_not_prove: Does not quantify what static K costs under DP; no cross-rank agreement mechanism exists in vLLM per this page.
bearing: Supports: load-adaptive speculation is turned OFF exactly in DP+EP MoE deployments; a gap in vLLM

title: [Bug]: vLLM hangs during speculative decoding with MoE draft model near max_model_len under Data Parallelism (DP) (issue #44185)
quote: When running vLLM with Speculative Decoding enabled, the server permanently hangs (deadlocks) under the following specific conditions:
proves: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, DP=2 + EP + MTP K=3: a request near max_model_len makes one DP rank skip drafting while the other enters the MoE drafter forward, so the collective never completes. Opened 2026-06-01, still open.
does_not_prove: A correctness bug, not a performance study; says nothing about the throughput cost of forcing all ranks to draft.
bearing: Supports: per-rank speculation decisions must be globally agreed under DP+EP; local choice deadlocks

title: Fix DP drafter hang near max model length (PR #44954)
quote: This PR fixes a vLLM hang during MTP speculative decoding with DP + EP near `max_model_len`.
proves: Fix for E4; notes the same issue was already fixed in vllm-ascend. Open (unmerged) as of today.
does_not_prove: No performance data; no general per-rank speculation-agreement design.
bearing: Same as E4: engines handle DP speculation by forcing uniformity

title: [Scheduler] Skip the spec + DP prefill-first MLP sync while no rank has prefill work (PR #42462)
quote: so a decode step pays two barriers instead of one
proves: With spec decode + DP attention, SGLang runs an extra prefill-first CPU all_gather each step so prefill and verify batches never mix across ranks. 8xB200 DeepSeek-V4-Flash DSpark ~50 req/rank: 2 gloo all_gathers/step, 9.4 ms waiting per 48.9 ms step (GPU kernels 21.9 ms). Skipping it when no rank has prefill: ~7% faster batch run (131 s -> 119-125 s). Open.
does_not_prove: Gain only when no rank has queued prefill (offline batch); continuous arrivals keep the barrier. Profiler inflates host time. Does not separate skew from acceptance vs skew from batch size.
bearing: Supports: speculation forces DP phase lockstep; the rank-skew barrier is a large share of step time

title: [Fix] spec: Remove `--speculative-skip-dp-mlp-sync` (PR #45043)
quote: the flag let one DP rank prefill while another decoded, which sent the decoding rank's batch into the prefill path, raised `AttributeError` and took the server down
proves: Merged 2026-10-18. The option that let spec-decode DP ranks run different phases was removed; the pre-sync now always runs unless SGLANG_ENABLE_DP_SPEC_PREFILL_COORDINATION is on.
does_not_prove: No performance numbers; does not describe how the coordination env var works.
bearing: Supports: decoupling DP ranks under speculation is still unsolved in SGLang as of last week

title: scheduler: opt-in DP-attention phase lockstep (--enable-dp-phase-lockstep) (PR #37273)
quote: generalizes the spec-decode path's prefill-first sync to non-spec serving
proves: Under DP attention any mixed decode+extend pass runs eager on every rank. Forcing phase lockstep (as spec decode already does) raised throughput 21-45% at c50-c200 on tp4/dp4 MoE with long prompts, TPOT p90 58->33 ms at c50.
does_not_prove: Non-spec workload; does not measure what lockstep costs spec decode when ranks have unequal acceptance or batch sizes.
bearing: Threatens a naive 'remove lockstep' idea: lockstep can be the faster design

title: Add DP-Draft to run draft model with TP=1 (PR #17418)
quote: For MoE drafts, EP=1 concentrates all experts on a single GPU and can lead to more fragmented kernel shapes, so throughput may not improve.
proves: Running the draft per-GPU at TP=1 while the target runs TP16/EP16 DP attention: Kimi-K2 4k/1.5k decode per GPU 1.87x at bs1 falling to 1.20x at bs32; on GSM8K Kimi-K2 DP-Draft 3173 tok/s vs 3466 no-draft (slower), DeepSeek-R1 NEXTN 3441 vs 3195 (faster). Closed unmerged.
does_not_prove: Speedup shrinks with batch; no tail or per-rank imbalance data; not adopted upstream.
bearing: Supports: drafter placement across DP ranks is a live design axis; speedup collapses at batch 32

title: [DSpark] Enable compact DP tier synchronization for PD decode (PR #37763)
quote: DSpark compact verification with DP Attention requires all participating DP ranks to select the same CUDA Graph verify tier.
proves: Verify CUDA-graph tier must be identical across DP ranks; on PD decode servers it was pinned (graph_tier=pinned), losing compact-verify benefit. PR gathers tier across ranks. Open.
does_not_prove: Speed numbers truncated in what I read; tier is a max over ranks, so per-rank verify width still cannot differ.
bearing: Supports: verify width is forced uniform across DP ranks; per-rank verify sizing is open

title: [Bug] EAGLE + DP attention: idle verify crashes (issue #43287)
quote: a DP rank that has no requests in a step crashes in the target verify
proves: Under EAGLE + DP attention an idle DP rank must still run a padded idle verify forward each step so collectives line up; a single in-flight request is enough to trigger the idle path.
does_not_prove: Bug report; no measurement of how much compute idle-rank verify padding wastes.
bearing: Supports: idle/light DP ranks pay full verify-shaped work; wasted-work accounting is open

title: [3/N] [spec] support STANDALONE spec decoding with DP attention (PR #30877)
quote: STANDALONE spec decoding and DP attention are mutually exclusive.
proves: As of 2026-07 separate-draft-model spec decode could not run with DP attention in SGLang; PR enables topk=1, attn_tp=1 only; Qwen3-30B-A3B + Qwen3-0.6B tp4/dp4 accept length 4.00 vs 3.95 without DP. Open.
does_not_prove: Correctness-only; no throughput or imbalance data; MoE drafts and PD untested.
bearing: Supports: DP + draft-model combos are immature; many configurations not even runnable

title: Eagle3 DP attention for Qwen3 MoE (PR #12002)
quote: Add eagle3 dp attention for Qwen3 MoE model for large scale EP deployment.
proves: Merged 2025-10-29. Shows a production-style decode config: EAGLE3 (3 steps, topk 3, 8 draft tokens) + DP attention + DeepEP low_latency + EPLB + --load-balance-method round_robin; 8xH100 GSM8K 565 tok/s.
does_not_prove: DP request placement is round_robin, blind to acceptance; no imbalance measurement.
bearing: Supports: DP dispatch in spec-decode deployments ignores acceptance

title: [v1] align execute_dummy_batch with uniform decode query length (PR #37142)
quote: When spec decode is enabled, `uniform_decode_query_len` becomes `1 + num_speculative_tokens`.
proves: In vLLM DP, idle ranks run dummy batches; with spec decode the dummy must be padded to 1+K tokens per request to match peers (DeepSeek-V3.2 + MTP + DP on B300). Closed unmerged.
does_not_prove: No cost measurement of padding idle ranks to verify shape.
bearing: Supports: idle-rank verify padding is real wasted work under DP

title: Accelerating SGLang with Multiple Token Prediction
quote: Data-Parallel Attention (DP Attention)
proves: MTP is integrated with DP attention, EPLB, DeepEP, TBO. Gains: +59.8% (3-token) / +60.8% (4-token) at 2 concurrent req per rank, accept length 2.18/2.44; only +14.2% at 128 concurrent req per rank. Advises draft size 2-3 under large batches.
does_not_prove: The two cases differ in hardware and settings; no per-DP-rank acceptance or imbalance data.
bearing: Supports: speculation gain shrinks with per-rank batch; DP-rank interaction unmeasured

title: DeepSeek-V3/R1 Inference System Overview (Day 6, open-infra-index)
quote: Uneven request counts and sequence lengths across DP instances cause disparities in core-attention computation
proves: DeepSeek runs three load balancers: prefill, decode (balance KV usage and request counts per GPU) and expert-parallel (minimize max dispatch receive load). Decode averages 20-22 tok/s per request, ~14.8k output tok/s per H800 node.
does_not_prove: The page does not mention MTP or acceptance; the decode LB balances request counts and KV, not tokens-per-step or acceptance.
bearing: Supports: production DP decode balancers are acceptance-blind

title: Pushing the Limits of Serving DeepSeek-V4-Pro
quote: DSpark traffic also exhibits significant expert skew.
proves: On H20 DP32-EP32 decode, they recorded routing from representative DSpark (speculative) requests and used it to configure EPLB and redundant experts: +13.5% per-GPU throughput. Also 319.92 -> 703.15 tok/s/GPU at 4K, 32 req per DP rank.
does_not_prove: Does not show that the skew is caused by verify tokens (vs plain decode); offline-profiled placement, not online.
bearing: Partly threatens 'verify-aware EPLB' as novel; supports: speculation-shaped expert skew is real and costly

title: Scaling Large MoE Models with Wide Expert Parallelism on NVL72 Rack Scale Systems
quote: In testing, large EP configurations reached up to 1.8x higher per-GPU throughput than smaller EP setups.
proves: TRT-LLM Wide-EP with online EPLB; EP32 vs EP8 comparison used disaggregated serving and MTP in both arms.
does_not_prove: MTP is held constant; no analysis of how MTP verify tokens change expert load or EPLB.
bearing: Neutral: confirms MTP + wide EP is standard, interaction unstudied

title: Utility-Driven Speculative Decoding for Mixture-of-Experts (Cascade)
quote: draft tokens collectively activate more weights, increasing data movement and verification time by 2-3x.
proves: In MoE, speculation can slow decode up to 1.5x; Cascade turns speculation on/off and tunes K by utility, limiting slowdown to 5% and +7-14% throughput vs static K.
does_not_prove: Single-node data movement view; nothing on EP all-to-all, per-rank receive load or DP.
bearing: Threatens 'MoE spec on/off by utility' as novel; leaves EP/DP version open

title: MoE-Spec: Expert Budgeting for Efficient Speculative Decoding
quote: large draft trees activate many unique experts, significantly increasing memory pressure
proves: Capping experts loaded per layer during verification gives 10-30% higher throughput than EAGLE-3.
does_not_prove: Abstract does not mention expert parallelism or batch size.
bearing: Threatens expert-budget verification ideas; EP-rank balance open

title: Less Experts, Faster Decoding: Cost-Aware Speculative Decoding for Mixture-of-Experts (EcoSpec)
quote: may route to disjoint experts, increasing expert-weight memory traffic
proves: Adds predicted marginal expert-activation cost to draft selection; up to 1.62x speedup.
does_not_prove: Abstract does not cover batched decoding or multi-GPU expert placement.
bearing: Threatens expert-aware draft selection; EP-rank load version open

title: Making Every Verified Token Count: Adaptive Verification for MoE Speculative Decoding (EVICT)
quote: expanding the union of activated experts and substantially increasing target-side verification cost
proves: Truncates draft tree using offline-profiled verification cost; up to 2.35x over AR, 1.21x avg over EAGLE-3; works in SGLang.
does_not_prove: Abstract does not address batching or EP.
bearing: Threatens tree-pruning-by-expert-cost ideas

title: XShare: Collaborative in-Batch Expert Sharing for Faster MoE Inference
quote: cuts peak GPU load by up to 3x in expert-parallel deployments
proves: In-batch expert sharing reduces expert activation up to 30% under standard batching, cuts peak per-GPU load up to 3x under EP, and gives up to 14% throughput in speculative decoding.
does_not_prove: Approximates routing (changes expert choice); not acceptance-aware; DP placement of requests not addressed.
bearing: Threatens 'reduce EP peak load under spec decode' ideas; closest prior art for verify-induced EP skew

title: Tackling the Data-Parallel Load Balancing Bottleneck in LLM Serving: Practical Online Routing at Scale (BalanceRoute)
quote: every decode step ends in a synchronization barrier whose latency is set by the most heavily loaded worker.
proves: DP decode imbalance compounds step after step into wasted compute; BalanceRoute online routing reduces DP imbalance and improves throughput on 144 NPUs vs vLLM.
does_not_prove: Abstract does not mention speculative decoding or variable tokens per step; no numbers in abstract.
bearing: Supports: acceptance-aware DP routing is unaddressed by the main DP-balance paper

title: NanoCP: Request-Level Dynamic Context Parallelism for Data-Expert Parallel Decoding
quote: this binding cannot balance both simultaneously, producing EP stragglers
proves: Routing to DP instance with smallest KV makes batch sizes unequal and EP stragglers; request-level dynamic CP gives 1.88-3.27x higher request rate under TPOT SLO and 1.79-2.12x lower P99.
does_not_prove: No mention of speculative decoding or MTP on the abstract page.
bearing: Supports: DP-EP decode balancing is active research but spec-blind

title: Nightjar: Dynamic Adaptive Speculative Decoding for Large Language Models Serving
quote: up to 14.76% higher throughput than standard speculative decoding
proves: Bandit planner disables speculation when not beneficial and offloads the draft to CPU when GPU memory is tight to grow KV/batch; up to 14.76% throughput and 20.18% latency gain (v5, 2026-06). Earlier version claimed 27.29%.
does_not_prove: Single-instance; no DP/EP, no cluster-level drafter scaling; numbers change across versions.
bearing: Threatens 'turn speculation off under load' and 'free drafter memory under load' as novel

title: TurboSpec: Closed-loop Speculation Control System for Optimizing LLM Serving Goodput
quote: the amount of successfully generated tokens
proves: Goodput-driven runtime choice of speculation level per batch in vLLM (v3 revised 2025-07).
does_not_prove: Abstract gives no numbers; single engine; no DP/EP.
bearing: Threatens goodput-based elastic speculation within one engine

title: How Speculative Decoding Boosts vLLM Performance by up to 2.8x
quote: As high QPS, we see 1.4x slowdown Llama3-70B on ShareGPT with 4xH100
proves: Speculation slows serving at high QPS: 1.4x (ShareGPT) and 1.8x (CNN/DailyMail) for Llama3-70B on 4xH100; dynamic spec decode shortens proposals under load.
does_not_prove: 2024 V0 numbers; dense model; no DP.
bearing: Supports the premise that speculation must be elastic with load

title: How we built production-ready speculative decoding with TensorRT-LLM
quote: we still observe steep performance drops when under high load.
proves: Baseten production: batching with spec decode failed (batch 2-3 where 10 expected); Llama 3.1 70B saw higher p50 with spec in one test; planned to adjust draft tokens by batch size.
does_not_prove: No numbers in text (charts are images); 2024; single replica.
bearing: Supports: production spec decode degrades under load

title: ATLAS: AdapTive-LeArning Speculator System
quote: The experiment is based on NVIDIA HGX B200 with batch-size 1, as detailed in Figure 1.
proves: Adaptive per-workload speculator plus controller that shortens lookahead or falls back to static; up to 500 TPS DeepSeek-V3.1, 460 TPS Kimi-K2 at batch 1 on B200.
does_not_prove: Batch 1 only; nothing on load, routing, or replica heterogeneity.
bearing: Leaves open: per-workload drafters across replicas and how the router uses them

title: Efficient Speculative Decoding for Llama at Scale: Challenges and Solutions
quote: our optimizations enable us to achieve a speed-up for large batch sizes between 1.4x and 2.0x at production scale.
proves: Meta EAGLE for Llama 4 Maverick: ~4 ms/token at batch 1 on 8xH100; 1.4-2.0x at large batch in production.
does_not_prove: Abstract says nothing on DP/EP balance, routing, or tail.
bearing: Threatens 'spec decode is useless at large batch' framing

title: Router Design (NVIDIA Dynamo docs)
quote: prefill_load_scale * adjusted_prefill_blocks
proves: Dynamo KV router picks the lowest cost worker from prefill blocks (minus overlap), potential decode blocks and active request blocks.
does_not_prove: Page does not mention speculative decoding, acceptance rate or draft tokens.
bearing: Supports: routers are acceptance-blind

title: Speculative Decoding (NVIDIA Dynamo docs v1.2.0)
quote: | vLLM | ✅ | Eagle3 draft model support |
proves: Dynamo spec decode support is vLLM Eagle3 only; SGLang and TRT-LLM marked not yet documented.
does_not_prove: No statement on router, planner/autoscaling or disaggregation interaction with speculation.
bearing: Supports: orchestration layer treats speculation as an engine detail

title: Predicted Latency-Based Scheduling for LLMs (llm-d blog)
quote: We assume all pods use the same accelerator class, a simplification that can be addressed in the future.
proves: XGBoost predicts TTFT/TPOT per pod from KV usage, input length, queue depth, running requests, prefix match, in-flight input tokens; ~5% MAPE; 43% better p50 E2E on Qwen3-480B MaaS workload.
does_not_prove: No speculation/acceptance feature; assumes uniform pods (so no heterogeneous drafters).
bearing: Supports: adding acceptance/drafter features to a TPOT predictor is open

title: vLLM Router: A High-Performance and Prefill/Decode Aware Load Balancer
quote: A low-overhead random-choice policy that provides excellent load distribution.
proves: vLLM Router policies: consistent hashing, power of two, round robin, random; P/D aware.
does_not_prove: No mention of speculative decoding, tokens per step or acceptance.
bearing: Supports: routers are acceptance-blind

title: On Evaluating Performance of LLM Inference Serving Systems
quote: this advantage can reverse at the tail (e.g., 1.16× higher P99 TPOT)
proves: Llama-3 70B 4xH100 0.25 QPS ShareGPT: spec decode 1.3x lower median TPOT but 1.16x higher P99 TPOT; higher TTFT from drafter prefill.
does_not_prove: Single low load point; does not attribute tail to per-request acceptance vs batch coupling; no DP.
bearing: Supports: acceptance-driven tail latency is real but unexplained

title: DSDE: Dynamic Speculative Decoding with KLD Stability for Real-World Serving
quote: adaptive speculation length cap to mitigate the straggler problem in per-sequence decoding
proves: Per-sequence K with a batch-level cap to limit stragglers in large-batch serving.
does_not_prove: No numbers in abstract; single engine; overlaps R04's adaptive-length coverage.
bearing: Threatens per-sequence-straggler ideas inside one batch

title: Semi-Clairvoyant Scheduling of Speculative Decoding Requests to Minimize LLM Inference Latency (LAPS-SD)
quote: LAPS-SD reduces inference latency by approximately 39%
proves: Request execution time depends on output length and acceptance rate; acceptance-aware priority queues cut latency ~39%.
does_not_prove: Single-server queue scheduling; not DP placement or cross-replica routing.
bearing: Partly threatens acceptance-aware scheduling; cross-rank placement open

title: NebulaSD: Many-for-Many Speculative Decoding
quote: organizes draft and target workers into independently schedulable resource pools
proves: Pools draft and target workers separately and rebuilds batches from shared request pools: +50.4% request-round rate vs physical disaggregation, +72.6% vs co-located, on 4 GPUs; simulated near-proportional scaling.
does_not_prove: 4-GPU testbed; idealized state movement in scaling sims; no autoscaling policy under bursty load.
bearing: Threatens 'scale drafter pool separately from target' as novel; elasticity policy left open

title: An Interpretable Latency Model for Speculative Decoding in LLM Serving
quote: explains why speedups often diminish as server load increases
proves: Analytical vLLM latency model with load-dependent and load-independent parts for prefill, drafting, verification; infers batch from request rate via Little's Law.
does_not_prove: No threshold or numbers in abstract; single replica.
bearing: Useful tool for an elasticity policy; threatens pure modeling contributions

title: Correctness Forensics for Batch Speculative Decoding: Diagnosing the Ragged Tensor Problem (EXSPEC)
quote: variable token acceptance desynchronizes position IDs, attention masks, and KV-cache across a batch.
proves: Grouping same-length sequences avoids realignment; 3x throughput at batch 8 on SpecBench.
does_not_prove: Grouping causes waiting (tail) per search snippet; I did not see tail numbers on the abstract page.
bearing: Supports: unequal acceptance creates coupling cost inside a batch

title: Adaptive Speculative Decoding (SGLang docs)
quote: The controller maintains independent EMA trackers for each batch size range
proves: SGLang adapts speculative_num_steps/num_draft_tokens at runtime per batch-size band; EAGLE/EAGLE3 topk=1 only.
does_not_prove: Page does not mention DP attention; E1 shows it is disabled there.
bearing: Background for E1/E2
